title: Singapore Police and Partners Prevent $17.4M Loss in Crypto Scam Crackdown
text: Singapore Police and Partners Prevent $17.4M Loss in Crypto Scam Crackdown A joint two-month operation by Singapore police, crypto exchanges, and international agencies identified and intervened to protect over 383 victims from losing $17.4 million to cryptocurrency scams, including impersonation and investment fraud. Through advanced blockchain analysis using tools, the authorities identified victims across multiple types of scams. Set as preferred sourcePolice, crypto exchanges and foreign agencies stopped more than 383 victims from losing over $17.4 million in a two-month scam crackdown. The fifth joint operation ran from Sept 1 to Oct 31 and used blockchain analysis, customer data and phone and in-person warnings to target fraud. Police said cross-border sharing with the FBI, NSW Police and the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre helped identify 32 foreign victims and will be expanded.SINGAPORE – More than 383 victims avoided losing over $17.4 million to cryptocurrency scams following a two-month joint crackdown by the police, digital payment token service providers, and foreign law enforcement agencies. The operation, which ran from Sept 1 to Oct 31, was the fifth blitz of its kind targeting crypto-related fraud, the police said in a statement on Nov 5.The operation was led by the police’s Cyber Command team, in partnership with DPT service providers including Coinbase, Coinhako, DTCPay, Gemini, Independent Reserve, OKX, StraitsX and Upbit. Through advanced blockchain analysis using tools from Chainalysis and TRM Labs, the authorities identified victims across multiple types of scams, including government officials impersonation, investment and job scams.The operation was also supported by customer information from the participating DPT service providers, which allowed officers to conduct targeted interventions over the phone and in person. The crackdown extended beyond Singapore, with the Cyber Command team sharing blockchain intelligence with foreign law enforcement partners, including the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation, Australia’s New South Wales Police Force and the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.This led to the identification of 32 foreign victims and allowed intervention efforts to be undertaken before further losses were incurred.“The outcome underscores the importance of sustained public-private partnership as well as timely cross-border intelligence sharing in combating scams,” the police said, adding that they will continue to expand its network of partners and deepen cooperation with foreign law enforcement agencies.by the police and several cryptocurrency exchanges prevented more than 355 victims from losing over $8.94 million.
